feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 6 (score 657.9) is the best measured result. Shortening body_length from 0.12 to 0.10 m at mass 0.6 kg moved the s-bend from 13 to 19 finishes, with line losses 0.55 and oscillation 0.33. The oval stayed at 20 of 20 with max_error 0.017 and oscillation 0.22. Iteration 5 showed the same pattern for the step before it (s-bend 2 to 13 finishes). So far the s-bend has responded to yaw inertia, and the oval has not been hurt. The slalom has not responded to any inertia change (0 of 20 finishes in iterations 5 and 6, progress about 0.23 to 0.26), which suggests its limit is separate from inertia. Read the next race as follows. If the s-bend reaches 19 or 20 finishes with line losses at or below 0.55 and oscillation stays under about 0.35 on the oval and s-bend, the mass step is working, and the next move is to test the controller or the slalom footprint. If s-bend steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35, restore mass to 0.6 kg, because body_length is already at its minimum and the inertia limit has been reached. If the slalom still shows 0 finishes with max_error at the floor, geometry alone is unlikely to fix it on this controller.
requested_changes: Keep body_length 0.10 and try mass 0.5 kg as proposed. If steering_oscillation on the s-bend or oval rises above about 0.35, restore mass to 0.6 kg, since iteration 6 gave s-bend oscillation 0.33 at mass 0.6 and the body length cannot go lower.

If the s-bend holds at 19 or more of 20 finishes and the slalom still has 0 finishes, try sensor y 0.075 with the same x positions, sensor_size 0.012 and wheel_track 0.09. Iteration 2 (y 0.07, wheel_track 0.10) gave slalom losses of 1.0, which is the best slalom result so far, and the oval has margin (max_error 0.017 at iteration 6).

If the slalom line losses stay near 1.85 (as at iteration 3, wheel_track 0.09) while the s-bend is at its limit, try wheel_track 0.095 as a compromise. Iteration 2 (0.10) gave s-bend progress 0.64 and slalom losses 1.0, while iteration 3 (0.09) gave s-bend progress 0.68 and slalom losses 1.85, so track width trades s-bend progress against slalom retention.
